analysis.hash_reuse: Canonical blob SHA-256 now also supplies SourceFingerprint.sha256 and the first-8-byte legacy blob alias. recovery_file_ref preserves its exact legacy digest while feeding path identity, colon, and text incrementally, avoiding a full concatenation allocation.
analysis.materialization: One owned UTF-8 payload remains required for validation, content detection, token/capsule generation, hashes, session metadata, and response ownership.
analysis.mmap: Not adopted: the response still requires owned UTF-8 text, while mmap would add concurrent truncation/atomicity hazards without eliminating response materialization. Fingerprinting instead streams through a fixed 64KiB buffer.
analysis.recovery: For a complete single on-disk file >=64KiB, the recovery blob and file records now store path/range/fingerprint metadata rather than duplicating the payload. Ranged, multi-file, small, shell, stdin, and ingest payloads retain inline/self-contained admission.
remaining_allocations: fail-open blob inline copy at recovery/lib.rs:1562
ordinary non-source-backed StoredFile copy at recovery/lib.rs:1590
analysis.staleness: Source-backed file expansion validates the persisted whole-file size/mtime/SHA-256 fingerprint; blob expansion validates its content-addressed hash. Changed or missing sources return stale-ref.
analysis.wall_time_follow_up: The first candidate redundantly SHA-256 hashed the 100MiB text for the source fingerprint after computing the identical canonical blob SHA, rehashed it for the legacy blob alias, and allocated format!(path:text) before hashing the file ref. Reusing the canonical digest and incrementally hashing path/colon/text reduced single wall 0.56->0.51s and four-way wall 0.690486->0.632006s. Residual differences versus baseline cannot be causally assigned because baseline is a pre-existing binary with unverified source; the optimized pointer path no longer performs an additional full fingerprint hash pass.

baseline_limitation: The baseline used a pre-existing release artifact whose source commit cannot be verified. Its binary SHA-256 and mtime are recorded in baseline.json; candidate provenance is a guarded build from the changed working tree. Deltas are reported without claiming a controlled same-commit rebuild.

before_after.loss: wall +0.12s after hash reuse (prior candidate 0.56s; baseline binary provenance is uncontrolled)
wall +0.16512s after hash reuse (prior candidate 0.690486s; baseline binary provenance is uncontrolled)

concurrent_ceiling.definition: sum of four /usr/bin/time -l per-process maxima; conservative because peaks need not coincide
